paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when Jesus is in the room, nothing you give Him is wasted. Mary pours out about a pint of expensive perfume, pure nard, on His feet (John 12:3). Judas calls it a waste and asks why it wasn't sold for three hundred denarii (John 12:5). Jesus says, "Leave her alone," and tells why she kept it: "in preparation for the day of My burial" (John 12:7).

Now look at the two hearts, because that's the real lesson. Judas sounded like he cared about the poor, but the text says he "was a thief" (John 12:6). Mary didn't give a speech. She just gave, and the whole house was filled with the fragrance (John 12:3). Jesus then says, "The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me" (John 12:8). I think that means some moments with Jesus are worth running toward, and they don't come around twice. And a heart can talk pretty and still be hiding something, but Jesus sees all of it.

Then the passage shows what Jesus does in people's lives. Many of the Jews were "deserting them and believing in Jesus" on account of Lazarus (John 12:11). The chief priests answered by making plans to kill Lazarus as well (John 12:10). So here's what I want you to take to your oven today, baker: give Jesus your best and don't apologize for it. Some people will call it too much, and Jesus will call it beautiful. I think I know whose opinion I'm baking for.
